stair-treads/palmetto.title: Palmetto FL Stair Treads | Matching Staircase Flooring
stair-treads/palmetto.description: Stair tread installation in Palmetto, FL for Trevesta and Artisan Lakes two-story homes and Snead Island elevated construction. 2026 pricing per tread.
stair-treads/palmetto.lede: Stair tread installation in Palmetto concentrates in Trevesta, Artisan Lakes and Snead Island's elevated custom homes, since most of the historic core and Riviera Dunes condos are single-level.
stair-treads/palmetto.capsule: Stair treads in Palmetto are mostly a Trevesta and Artisan Lakes job: two-story builder plans built since the 2010s make up most of the staircases we match to new flooring. Old Palmetto's bungalows and most Riviera Dunes condo units are single-level, so stair work there is the exception rather than the rule. Typical 2026 installed ranges run $55 to $220 per tread.
stair-treads/palmetto.body_html:
Most of the stair tread work we do in Palmetto traces back to Trevesta and Artisan Lakes, the city's two newer inland communities, where two-story floor plans built since roughly 2010 are common and a main-floor flooring replacement almost always means matching the stairs to whatever's going in below. A 1,900 sq ft two-story Trevesta home replacing carpet with LVP downstairs would typically need thirteen to fifteen treads plus a matching stair nose transition where the new floor meets the landing.

The rest of the city looks different. Old Palmetto and the historic district are mostly single-story 1900s-1960s bungalows and block homes on modest lots, houses that were never built with a second floor, so interior stair work there is rare and usually limited to a porch step or an exterior entry rather than a full staircase. Riviera Dunes runs the same way for a different reason: most of the condo units in the marina-front towers are single-level, even though the buildings themselves run many stories tall, so an individual owner's flooring job almost never includes interior stairs. Snead Island's custom homes are the exception within the waterfront market, since a number of them are built on two or three levels to clear flood elevation requirements near the Manatee River, and those staircases get the same wide-plank hardwood or engineered oak tread going into the rest of the house.

Material choice on a Palmetto staircase usually follows whatever's already decided for the main floor rather than getting picked separately. A Trevesta or Artisan Lakes home going with laminate downstairs typically gets laminate treads to match, while a Snead Island house getting wide-plank engineered oak gets solid or engineered hardwood treads instead of a vinyl stair nose that would look out of place against the rest of the flooring. Vinyl plank stairs hold up fine day to day but need a proper stair nose profile, not just plank cut to fit, or the leading edge wears through faster than the rest of the tread.
stair-treads/palmetto.cost_html:
A thirteen-tread Trevesta staircase in LVP at $65-$105 per tread runs $845-$1,365 installed, plus risers if the client wants them finished to match rather than left painted, at $25-$65 each ($325-$845), for a total of roughly $1,170-$2,210.

A Snead Island staircase in solid hardwood to match a wide-plank main floor runs $130-$220 per tread, so a fifteen-tread run comes to $1,950-$3,300, noticeably more than the LVP equivalent because of both material and the extra fitting time solid wood treads take. Engineered hardwood treads split the difference at $110-$180 per tread. Full pricing is on our stair treads cost guide.

faqs.q: Do most Palmetto homes have interior stairs that need treads?
faqs.a: Not in the historic core. Old Palmetto's bungalows are mostly single-story, and most Riviera Dunes condo units are single-level despite living in a multi-story building. Stair tread work concentrates in Trevesta, Artisan Lakes and Snead Island's elevated custom homes instead.

faqs.q: Why are some Snead Island homes built with multiple levels and interior stairs?
faqs.a: A number of custom homes there are built up to clear flood elevation requirements near the Manatee River, which means an interior staircase and treads that typically match whatever wide-plank hardwood or engineered oak is going into the main living areas.

faqs.q: Should my Trevesta stair treads match the flooring I'm installing downstairs?
faqs.a: Yes, that's what most owners choose. A laminate or LVP main floor usually gets matching treads with a proper stair nose profile, since mismatched material on the staircase tends to stand out more than owners expect once it's installed.
